goal: Open on the real doctor explaining the test, then earn the viewer's trust with Bayes' theorem worked on that very test — 90 seconds, narrated.
audience: a patient who just got a positive result and does not know what it means
assumptions: 90 seconds total: the clip is the cold open (~10s), the Bayes example the body (~80s)
the Bayes numbers are computed claims (sympy), the clip's words are real footage
the example uses the test's own numbers if the clip states them, else a clearly-labeled typical example
the language follows the request: English
no format was named: the plan states its assumption (16:9)
narrated: a spoken voice carries the explanation
the doctor clip is missing: flagged in feasibility; the plan keeps both the open (edit) and the body (math)

decision.why: The piece needs what no single technique has: real footage for the doctor (edit) and a narrated, verified derivation for Bayes (math — the numbers must be computed claims, the narration must drive the scenes). The edit-film assembler joins them with a designed transition.

alternatives.rejected_because: a Bayes explainer without the real doctor loses the reason to care — the clip IS the hook
the derivation cannot be cut from footage we do not have; a captioned formula over the doctor would be neither verified nor narrated

alternatives.id: simplest: the clip plus on-screen text of the result
alternatives.rejected_because: the simplest thing that could work — but 'explain Bayes' theorem' asks for the worked example, and worked means computed

segments.role: the cold open: the real doctor
segments.brief: The clip of the doctor explaining the test: cut to its strongest 10 seconds, captioned in the studio's design, ending on the question the example will answer.
acceptance: the piece opens on the real doctor clip (a cold open, the actual footage)
Bayes' theorem is explained with a worked example (real numbers computed on screen)
the math is verified: the theorem statement and the example are sympy claims
the example's numbers are honest: hypothetical inputs are labeled as such
narrated: a spoken voice carries the explanation

segments.brief: Bayes on the test: the prior, the test's sensitivity and specificity (computed claims), the posterior — the number the patient actually wants, narrated.
acceptance: every number is a sympy-verified claim
the narration clock drives the scenes
the posterior lands as the payoff
